europe_now.title: Spanish Economist Tapped to Head ECB
europe_now.summary: EU leaders have cleared the path for Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos to succeed Christine Lagarde as president of the European Central Bank. The appointment marks a significant leadership transition for the eurozone's monetary authority.

sources.headline: Spain’s Hernández de Cos tapped to succeed fellow ‘owl’ Lagarde as ECB president
Spanish economist de Cos to succeed Lagarde as head of ECB

europe_now.title: Poland Orders Alternative Constitutional Court Financing
europe_now.summary: The Polish prime minister has ordered an alternative financing channel for the constitutional court after the central bank froze its accounts. The move highlights ongoing institutional friction and funding disputes within the country.

sources.headline: Polish PM orders alternative financing channel for constitutional court after central bank freezes accounts

top_stories.title: New UK-EU Consultative Arrangements
top_stories.summary: The United Kingdom is set to receive Swiss-style consultative rights under newly negotiated arrangements with the European Union. These deals aim to establish structured dialogue mechanisms between British and European officials.

sources.headline: UK to get ‘Swiss-style’ consultative rights under new EU deals

top_stories.title: Spanish Electoral Campaign Dynamics
top_stories.summary: Spain is experiencing heightened political mobilization and public debate concerning housing and the rise of far-right political forces ahead of an upcoming snap election. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has emphasized the importance of high voter turnout to secure a progressive majority.
